rationale: Start with a broad gradient to observe all ten compounds and locate the elution window and limiting pairs. A 10-minute gradient balances initial separation against the penalty for late elution.

Change only gradient duration to test whether the two limiting pairs respond to a shallower slope. The current last peak at 7.16 minutes leaves room to improve separation while targeting elution within 10 minutes.

The limiting pair improved strongly with a shallower gradient, so reduce the slope further while raising the starting organic fraction to offset the added retention time. The first peak previously eluted near 0.13 organic, so this also tests how much the early separation tolerates trimming the gradient window.

Injection 3 reached the maximum CRF; now test a shorter fully resolved method by shifting the gradient window upward while preserving its 0.05 organic-fraction/min slope. This should advance the last peak by about one minute, with early-peak resolution the main risk to check.

Keep injection 4’s gradient fixed and raise temperature to test selectivity at its sole limiting pair while shortening retention. Injection 3 remains the maximum-score fallback if heating does not restore full resolution.

Test the maximum temperature using injection 3’s fully resolved gradient to seek earlier elution with altered selectivity. Returning to 0.15 initial organic should protect early-pair retention and resolution as heating shortens the run.

Test 55 C as a selectivity compromise: it may separate the near-coincident middle pair seen at 60 C while retaining enough temperature-driven separation in the other crowded region. Keep the gradient unchanged from injections 3 and 6 to isolate this effect.

Make the gradient modestly shallower to improve the nearly resolved pair at 55 C while preserving early retention. The last peak at 8.54 minutes leaves time for this adjustment without exceeding the 10-minute scoring threshold.
Use a slope halfway between injections 7 and 8 to shorten the fully resolved run. Interpolation suggests both limiting pairs will retain R above 1.5, with the last peak near 9 minutes.

Test a cooler, steeper gradient for a shorter fully resolved alternative: cooling may move the crowded middle peaks away from the selectivity crossover seen on heating. The shorter gradient should offset increased retention; injection 9 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Test a substantially faster gradient at 60 C, where the middle-pair elution order appears to have crossed relative to 55 C. Steepening may separate that pair on the opposite side of the crossover while substantially advancing the last peak.

Test a lower starting organic fraction with a faster gradient at 55 C to shift middle-pair selectivity while maintaining early-peak retention. This explores whether full resolution can be retained with a substantially earlier last peak than injection 9.

Shorten injection 12’s gradient while keeping its starting composition and temperature fixed to test the speed limit of this promising selectivity regime. Both limiting pairs are close to threshold, so this run will establish whether faster elution preserves full resolution.

Test modest cooling relative to injection 1 to move its limiting cluster away from co-elution without lengthening the gradient. Using 35 C rather than 30 C may avoid the additional close pairs seen in the colder run while targeting full resolution near seven minutes.

Test the low-temperature endpoint for a distinct elution-order regime beyond the crowded patterns at 30–35 C. The broad, fast gradient should keep the last peak below 10 minutes while revealing whether these selectivity crossovers open a faster fully resolved option.

At 60 C, steepening improved the limiting middle pair between injections 6 and 11; test a still steeper gradient to pursue that trend. Lower the starting organic fraction to protect early retention and potentially recover separation in the compressed middle cluster.

Return to the successful 55 C regime and test a modestly higher starting fraction with a shallower slope to compensate for its selectivity effect. This targets full resolution near injection 12’s retention time, potentially with better margins at the limiting pairs.

With the maximum CRF already secured, explore a substantially faster gradient at an intermediate temperature for a different middle-cluster selectivity pattern. The low starting organic fraction protects early retention, while this run tests whether full resolution is possible on the steeper-gradient side of the observed crossovers.

Preserve injection 12’s successful slope of 0.075 organic-fraction/min but end the programmed gradient sooner. Its last peak eluted near 0.57 organic, so all ten peaks should retain their full resolution and approximately 7.60-minute last retention time before the new gradient ends.

Slightly flatten injection 17’s gradient to lift its R = 1.47 pair above threshold while retaining the other limiting pair’s separation. This targets another maximum-score method with more balanced resolution margins and a last peak comfortably below 10 minutes.
Use a gradient slope between injections 17 and 20, targeting R just above 1.5 for both limiting pairs. This should shorten injection 20’s separation while preserving the maximum CRF.

Test a shallower version of injection 4 to recover its sole unresolved pair while retaining the time saving from the higher starting organic fraction. This explores another maximum-score option below 10 minutes, with stronger early-pair retention than the high-temperature methods.

Test a slightly shallower version of injection 8 to seek a larger minimum-resolution margin while retaining maximum CRF. Extrapolation puts the last peak near 10 minutes, so this probes the time-penalty boundary.

Use a slope between injections 8 and 9 to balance their two limiting pairs, targeting a minimum resolution near 1.7. The last peak should remain below 10 minutes, preserving maximum CRF with a larger separation margin than the fastest method.

Trim injection 24’s gradient window while keeping nearly the same slope, targeting its balanced resolution margins with a shorter programmed gradient. The last peak previously eluted near 0.54 organic, so a 0.60 endpoint should keep every peak within the gradient and preserve maximum CRF.
